Reuse master's remaining selection-shadow and cumulative-promotion proof when landed with exact matching contracts. Add only audio-specific counterexamples: external corpus/model bindings, production-training subprocesses, oracle captures and raw-waveform/session/HTTP integration. Preserve conservative scope until independence is proved; historical zero-reuse full gates are cost observations, not evidence that a narrower policy is safe. Attribute verifier preparation, internally repeated training/resource probes, outer deterministic repeat agreement and package execution separately. Review redundant work on the same audio obligations without changing frozen verify-classifier-v1, inserting artificial device/seed markers, or weakening exact-resume, fault-detection and final integration checks. Any new classifier contract must preserve historical replay through the shared owner. Include the early harness-ratchet counterexample recorded in finding evidence:sha256:1336ee039ad2e2ed79edb4b0e988b2dadbad6d9b56003fd2191b8db4587578bc. Exercise change-specific selection on isolated witness diffs for plan-only changes, host audio math, buffer ownership, shared CUDA/ABI, optimizer/checkpoint and serving contracts. Assert inclusion of actual dependent runtime files/subprocesses and exclusion only when independence is established. Report derived selection reasons and executed/reused/inapplicable checks; a broad shared executor change can legitimately require a broad gate. Reuse existing shared admission so CPU checks do not hold an exclusive GPU reservation; correctness may share admitted capacity, while performance remains exclusive. The attempted 27-to-15 row consolidation after merge 476565f7 preserved all 35 verifier commands but was refused by protected-plan membership; keep those identities pending, not completed. items.title: Publish through one store path: idempotent writes, verified content fill, alias-local preconditions

steps.title: Publish through one store path: idempotent writes, verified content fill, alias-local preconditions
steps.rationale: Integrity and blocking first. A store that already holds a bare descriptor refuses the later batch carrying its content (artifactFacet.validate), which blocks lane outcomes; 66420d36 avoids new bare records but repairs none. Build on the commit coordinator (commit_coordinator.go:44) so every caller shares idempotent publication, content verification, alias compare-and-set and conflict reporting. Treat descriptor-exists and content-available as distinct states, with one supported path to fill an existing descriptor with matching, verified content. A caller declares whether its decision depends on the whole head. Alias-local operations take only their alias precondition, so unrelated writers do not invalidate them. Keep expensive preparation outside the write lock. Done when the bare-record repair works, the per-caller publication and retry code is deleted, and writer wait is measured before and after.

items.title: Bound peak memory at the store's copying points

steps.title: Bound peak memory at the store's copying points
steps.rationale: Three measured points; the first, pack construction and verification, lands as pack-streams-members. Checkpoint creation serializes, restores and serializes a projection again to prove canonical form (checkpoints.go:57); retention copies catalog and graph state before computing reachability (retention.go:72). Share one bounded entry-reading and hashing path between lookup and verification, stream packs through the existing atomic publication, bound checkpoint concurrency, and traverse retention over the smallest stable representation. Keep every integrity check. Done when peak memory stays bounded as payload volume grows, with index memory accounted separately.

items.title: Land one finished row from a tree that holds another

steps.title: Land one finished row from a tree that holds another
steps.rationale: Residual of landing-one-path. On 2026-09-24 two finished rows in one tree could not land one at a time: scope refuses any unshipped verification input, so one row's files were copied aside and restored by hand, twice. A gate that measured and verified only its candidate (HEAD plus its paths), with every admission-time read taken from that candidate, could admit unshipped work safely. Low priority while one row at a time is in flight. Done when a path-scoped landing passes beside unrelated unshipped Go, and every check it runs reads the candidate.

items.title: Make preflight and the commit gate two stages of one execution

steps.title: Make preflight and the commit gate two stages of one execution
steps.rationale: Preflight runs the gate's own static check definitions (about 20 s measured 2026-09-24: modern-go 16.6 s, architecture 4.5 s, the rest under 3 s each), and the gate then repeats them against the frozen candidate; the gate already reuses its own earlier passes through the retry cache. The obstacle measured 2026-09-24: gate checks are bound to the manifest plan of the frozen candidate (bindCheckExecution in verification.go), and cache slots key on the bound invocation, which preflight does not compute; computing the manifest plan in preflight costs the gate's planning time (about 24 s), so sharing needs a reuse key on the unbound check and its input fingerprint, validated against the bound invocation at the gate. Only loop -land runs preflight; a direct gate saves nothing. Done when an unchanged candidate repeats no pure static check after a preflight, and a changed input invalidates exactly its checks.

items.title: Share claim mechanics across locks while keeping each resource's rules

steps.title: Share claim mechanics across locks while keeping each resource's rules
steps.rationale: processlock, authoritylock, device resource jobs, the gate lanes lock and plan row claims each record and report holders their own way. Measured 2026-09-24 (read-only survey): the repeats are in acquisition and probing, not liveness -- create-directory-and-acquire in authoritylock, the lanes runner and the campaign lock; an acquire-and-close busy probe in three places; PID liveness layered on an OS lock in the campaign lock and an unread PID in gate_lanes.json; holder naming only in processcontrol and fsatomic. Sharing them (processlock.AcquireState, Held, a BusyError that names holders through fsatomic) removes about 45 production lines. Risks: a probe briefly holds the lock and can make a racing acquirer see busy; merging the Windows cancellation bridges risks use-after-free. The exclusive GPU claim cannot release before process exit (a job object cannot drop a process), so "release when ownership ends" does not hold for it without a different claim design. Done when the shared helpers replace the repeats, the PID liveness is deleted, and a cross-process test shows a process releasing a lock, staying alive, and the next owner proceeding.

steps.title: Store gate telemetry and merge authority by reference

A merge landing re-embeds the audited completions and retirements of every earlier merge (673 KB, 88% repeated; projected_merge_authority.go:175). Group suite rows under their package; store the reader graph as its own content that the cause references; have merge authority reference the previous authority and store only the entries since. Readers accept the old shapes. Done when each document stores only what changed since its predecessor, and the repeated copies are deleted from the writers.

items.title: Cut the gate suite's longest tests

steps.title: Cut the gate suite's longest tests
steps.rationale: Measured 2026-09-23 at 83d0bb9b: suite 149-155 s. The critical path is the live fixture's single lock: ready at about 33 s, then 14 seeded plans run one at a time for about 103 s, and TestTestingReductionContract's five plans end the suite alone. Each plan recomputes whole-snapshot analyses for a one-file seed (codeprofile.Build 14 s, the consumer graph through go list 15 s, manifest identity 10 s and diff 6 s, CPU over five plans), so the content-keyed manifest cache never hits. Warming the base manifest in the fixture measured no gain. A pool of checkouts costs about 40 s of cold setup per extra slot and reverses the one-checkout budget. The structural lever is incremental analysis keyed per file or package (profile facts and consumer-graph edges reused for unchanged files), which also shortens every production gate's base-versus-candidate manifests.

items.title: Re-source the Gemma 12B checkpoint (owner decision: download)

steps.title: Re-source the Gemma 12B checkpoint (owner decision: download)
steps.rationale: OWNER DECISION: download the unquantized google/gemma-4-12B-it checkpoint? The instruction-framing premise is falsified, and the runtime is cleared. Measured 2026-09-24: on the guard corpus's SHORT shape at byte offsets 0/20107/60322, the 12B twins (both converted from the third-party vrfai ModelOpt FP8 quant, models/gemma-4-12B-it-fp8) score raw NLL 8.5/8.0/1.2-1.4 against E4B's 6.5/6.1/0.6, and chat framing (tmp/chat_rung.go) leaves them 0.5-1.2 nats worse everywhere. On a plain English paragraph the 12B scores 3.17 nats per token against E4B's 1.48. overgo's 12B graph matches the transformers gemma4_unified reference point by point (value from the raw key projection with an unscaled v_norm on k_eq_v global layers, 25% proportional rope, one global KV head, attention scale 1, layer scalar, final softcap 30): layer outputs agree within 2.6e-4 of a Go transcription of the reference layer, GPU agrees with the host executor, the runner agrees with a 48-layer host chain, logits agree with adaptive_new's transformers golden within about 0.2, and the GGUF matches the safetensors. So transformers would score these weights the same, and the leading suspect is the FP8 quant itself. Probes are in tmp (g4_layer_ref.go, g4_host_nll.go, g4_golden.go, g4_gguf_vs_st.go, g4_fp8_scale.go, chat_rung.go). Next, with the owner's yes: convert the bf16 checkpoint and run tmp/chat_rung.go and g4_host_nll.go on it; if it scores at or below E4B, retire or re-source the FP8 12B twins. Done when a 12B checkpoint scores no worse than E4B on the same windows, held by TestGemmaTwelveScoresNoWorseThanE4B.
